title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks capped a volatile week with a Friday rally - S&P 500 +0.5% to 7,743.41, Nasdaq +0.5% to 27,068.72, Dow +0.9% (478 pts) to 51,828.62 - as yields and oil eased.

Markets: Treasury yields retreated off intraweek highs - 2-year fell to 4.86%, 10-year settled the week at 5.18% (had topped 5.2% midweek); Brent crude dropped ~2% to $104.32 on Hormuz reopening hopes.
Markets: Gold rose to ~$4,320/oz and Bitcoin held near $84,000 as bond-market volatility stayed elevated.
Companies: Microsoft (+3%) led the Dow; chip/AI names rallied (Micron, ON Semiconductor, PHLX Semiconductor index +1.4%).
Companies: Akamai Technologies (+3%) signed an $11B+, seven-year cloud-services deal with Anthropic; Genius Sports jumped 13% after JPMorgan initiated coverage at overweight.
Macro/Policy: US-Iran talks reportedly touched on a phased Strait of Hormuz reopening in exchange for ending the US naval blockade, though skepticism remains that a deal is imminent.

Macro/Policy: Final September University of Michigan consumer sentiment came in at 48.1, down 7% from August but slightly above the 47.8 consensus; Xi's Washington visit produced no trade breakthrough on Taiwan.
Macro/Policy: Week ahead brings the September jobs report, PCE inflation, Case-Shiller home prices and durable goods, plus Fed speakers Williams, Goolsbee and Logan.
